A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GOC study. All 10 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables and references, support comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original GOC experiments on ImageNet and MS-COCO, including quality scores, ablations, hyperparameter sweeps, generated images and latency results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and additionally reports FLOPs and relative speed in Table 3.

M1.justification: Equation (8) changes GOD's time term from gamma*t/T to gamma*(1-t/T), retaining the B(t)<Gamma selection condition. This revises the documented gating rule; the gradient queue, extrapolation and feature-statistics components remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether the implementation changed.

E1.justification: Both evaluate ImageNet class-conditional generation and MS-COCO text-to-image synthesis using DiT and Pixart. Removing illustrative prompts from Figure 5 does not establish a change to the benchmark evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: Section 4.1 already identifies v1's TC as reproduced Learning-to-Cache and RC as an implementation based on FORA. v2 renames these L2C and FORA; corresponding comparisons retain the same methods and GC/GOC configurations.

E3.justification: Table 3 adds FLOPs and relative-speed evaluation metrics. The stated protocols otherwise retain 20 denoising steps, DDIM for DiT, DPM-Solver for Pixart, 50,000/30,000 samples, 256×256 resolution and the same caching levels.

E4.justification: Figure 5 removes the vase and bathroom qualitative comparisons, retaining the train and refrigerator examples. The GC/GOD ablations, single-step versus cumulative analysis and eta sensitivity sweep remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Table 5 retains the same timing values with ± quantities. Neither version adds run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or explanations of uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Existing numerical quality and latency results are retained. Table 3 adds compute/speed entries, including 5.934 TFLOPs and 1.9999× speed for 50% FORA+GOC. Figure 5 removes two qualitative result triplets, and Section 4.4 replaces the vase observation with a train observation.

T1.justification: Equation (3) replaces independent residual expressions using x with sequential self-attention, cross-attention and MLP dependencies, also identifying the MLP output with x at t+1. Equation (8) revises the defined gating score. The remaining mathematics is retained, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: gradient compensation reduces caching errors, statistical and temporal gating limits gradient errors, and GOC improves generation quality with negligible overhead.

C2.justification: Both retain the explanations of late-step error accumulation, the interpretation of eta sensitivity and complementarity with learned caching, and the limitations concerning fixed parameters and bound steps. The added FLOPs discussion reiterates the existing negligible-overhead interpretation.

D1.justification: v2 adds a stated GOC code-availability link in the abstract, absent from v1. Existing hardware, sampling settings, baseline implementation provenance and hyperparameter information remain. Repository availability or contents cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds background citations, including Error-Optimized Cache and several multimodal/few-shot works, removes the PAB discussion and reference, and explicitly distinguishes SmoothCache's module selection from correcting existing errors. The main positioning relative to FORA and learned caching remains.

P1.justification: v2 standardizes RC/TC terminology to FORA/L2C, edits the motivation and several experimental paragraphs, consolidates author information and adds acknowledgements. The section hierarchy and overall narrative remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: Tables are restyled and Table 3 gains two columns. Figure 1 moves from page 2 to page 1; Figure 5 moves from page 9 to page 8 and changes from four example triplets to two. The author block is compressed, while most visual content is retained.

improvement.justification: The new code link, clearer comparator labels and Table 3 compute reporting improve documentation. However, Equation (8) reverses the time weighting while retaining the selection condition, late-step rationale and quality results. The PDFs do not explain whether this corrects the description or changes the procedure underlying those results. This unresolved connection between method and evidence prevents a reliable net-quality judgment.
